text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- ING Bank will arrange a $160 million syndicated letter of credit for Romania's electricity authority Renel.
ADEVARUL
- The 1996 state budget deficit exceeds 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, compared with 2.2 percent agreed under loan accords with the International Monetary Fund.
- Gheorghe Crainiceanu, first vice-president of Banca Romaneasca, said the inter-bank market was confronted with an acute hard currency shortage.
- The government to be appointed after the November 3 polls will have to take steps to fight inflation, central bank chief economist Daniel Daianu said.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Banking experts predict the leu will trade at around 4,500 to the dollar by end-1996, which means a 50 percent depreciation compared with the rate at the start of the year.
ZIUA
- CEC savings bank will give loans worth 120 billion lei for housing construction this year.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- President Ion Iliescu is supported by nine percent of voters in Transylvania, according to a regional opinion poll commissioned by the Soros Foundation in Cluj.
- A school in the western city of Timisoara resorted to bodyguards to prevent violence and burglary.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu heads a delegation to the Black Sea Economic Cooperation conference in Moscow.
- Opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) leader Emil Constantinescu pledged to sack the Prosecutor General if he is elected president, in a bid to fight corruption.
- According to CDR, the ruling Party of Social Democracy would need 17,000 billion lei per year to finance its electoral programme.
- Partial results or exit polls are banned from being released on election day, November 3, before polling stations close, the broadcasting authority says.
ADEVARUL
- IRSOP pollster will released a forecast on election day at 9 p.m., right after polling stations close.
- The main opposition parties are expected to sign on Monday a technical agreement for supervising both parliamentary and presidential elections.
LIBERTATEA
- The Interior Ministry is to auction off a Renault 16 which belonged to executed stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's wife.
- Prime Minister Vacaroiu is satisfied with the achievements of his government, saying the cabinet has managed to keep the budget balanced.
CRONICA ROMANA

- Sindic judge Ioan Georgiu is expected to call a general shareholders meeting to debate proposals to restructure troubled Dacia Felix SA bank and raise its share capital. ($= 3,332 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
